## What the truncation costs, in days {visibility="uncounted"}

![](../figures/delays-right-truncation.png){width="72%"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Two panels. On the left, the delay distribution seen by day 7
and by day 14 sits well to the left of the true distribution. On the
right, the mean estimated delay rises from under 2 days towards the
true mean of 5.9 days as the cutoff moves away from now, passing 3.9
days at a cutoff of 7 and 5.3 days at a cutoff of 14."}

- The shortfall grows the nearer the cutoff is to now
- A mean of **3.9 days rather than 5.9** is what the forecast and the
  transmission model are handed

::: {.attribution}
`LogNormal(1.6, 0.6)` with daily windows, computed for this talk with
`CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22,
`scripts/delays-right-truncation.jl`
:::

## Eighteen branches, or the type you passed {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```stan
real dist_lcdf(real delay, array[] real params,
               int dist_id) {
  if (dist_id == 1)
    return lognormal_lcdf(delay | params[1], params[2]);
  else if (dist_id == 2)
    return gamma_lcdf(delay | params[1], params[2]);
  // ... 15 more branches ...
  else if (dist_id == 25)
    return von_mises_lcdf(delay | params[1], params[2]);
  else reject("Invalid distribution identifier: ",
              dist_id);
}
```

- And a second table of 10, saying which of those 18 have positive
  support
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```julia
primarycensored_cdf(dist::Gamma, primary_event::Uniform,
    x::Real, ::AnalyticalSolver)

primarycensored_cdf(dist::LogNormal, primary_event::Uniform,
    x::Real, ::AnalyticalSolver)

primarycensored_cdf(dist::Weibull, primary_event::Uniform,
    x::Real, ::AnalyticalSolver)

primarycensored_cdf(dist::D1, primary_event::D2,
    x::Real, method::NumericSolver
) where {D1 <: UnivariateDistribution,
         D2 <: UnivariateDistribution}
```

- **Three closed forms** picked by the type you passed, and one
  fallback for any `UnivariateDistribution`
- In Stan `Frechet` needs a new branch, a new integer and a rebuild
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
`primarycensored_ode.stan:52-77` ·
`primarycensored_cdf.jl:184-201`, `:323`, `:373`, `:415`, v0.2.22
:::

## Everything I tried in between {visibility="uncounted"}

![](../figures/delays-stan-failures.png){width="80%"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Horizontal bar chart of ten runs reported in
epinowcast/primarycensored issue 34. The first, integrate_1d at
tolerance 1e-6, lost 243 of 256 chains. Eight tuning attempts sit
between 12 and 27 per cent, one of them a model with the truncation
adjustment removed. The last, recast as ode_rk45, lost 0 of 600."}

::: {.attribution}
Every run is one Sam Abbott reported in
[epinowcast/primarycensored#34](https://github.com/epinowcast/primarycensored/issues/34)
between 5 and 12 September 2024, read back from the issue,
`scripts/delays-stan-failures.py`. The runs are not one dataset. The
scenario was made harder in the same PR that landed the ODE, so the
last two rows on 600 chains are the pair closest to like for like.
:::

## The observation process is the type {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```julia
julia> typeof(double_interval_censored(
           Gamma(2.0, 3.0); upper = 15, interval = 1))

IntervalCensored{
  Truncated{
    PrimaryCensored{
      Gamma{Float64},
      Uniform{Float64},
      AnalyticalSolver{GaussLegendre{…}}}}}
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
- The tree is the type. Nothing dispatches on a name or an integer, so
  there is nothing to keep in step
- Swap `Gamma` for any `UnivariateDistribution` and the rest of the
  tree is unchanged
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
Real output, `CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22. Reflowed onto several
lines, and the type parameters of the solver and of `Truncated` are
elided at `…`
:::

## The numerical problem moved, it did not go away {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}
| Autodiff backend | Broken |
|---|---:|
| ForwardDiff | 0 |
| ReverseDiff, tape | 0 |
| Mooncake forward | 3 |
| Mooncake reverse | 3 |
| Enzyme forward | 4 |
| Enzyme reverse | 8 |

::: {.attribution}
Scenarios registered broken out of 63, in
`test/ADFixtures/src/ADFixtures.jl`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="56%"}
- **Six autodiff backends**, each with its own CI workflow. Two of them
  pass every scenario, four carry scenarios registered broken
- The default solver is **`GaussLegendre(; n = 64)`** because fixed
  nodes trace through all six backends and adaptive ones do not
- Stan gave up adaptive quadrature for an ODE. Julia gave it up for a
  dot product
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
Six per-backend workflows in `.github/workflows/`, over a shared
`ad-backend.yaml` · why an ecosystem needs that CI was the 14:30 talk
